# Editing Notes

The craft survives in the old advice. As one editor put it, "Short
sentences carry the reader further than long ones, and the editor's
first duty is to cut what the reader never asked to read", per the
[notes on editing](./source.html).

A tampered memory drifts one word: "the editor's first duty is to
trim what the reader never asked to read", per the same
[notes](./source.html).

An invented line reads well and proves nothing: "an editor owes the
reader a clean page and a short apology for the rest", again per the
[notes](./source.html).

An unsourced one stands alone: "every quotation must survive a trip
back to its source before the document ships."

The maxim carries the whole book: "A checker that never lies beats
one that catches more but sometimes lies", from the
[maxim itself](./source.html#:~:text=A%20checker%20that%20never%20lies).
